children: Michael Leiters tells employees the existing restructuring plan remains unchanged after reports suggested another 4,100 positions could be eliminated
Porsche CEO Michael Leiters has told employees that the company has no plans for an additional 4,000 job cuts, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters.

Leiters was responding to a Handelsblatt report that Volkswagen’s supervisory board viewed around 4,100 additional positions at Porsche as surplus, beyond the job reductions already agreed as part of the luxury carmaker’s restructuring.

“There are no plans to cut an additional 4,000 jobs at Porsche,” Leiters said in the memo, adding that the company’s existing restructuring programme had been approved by Porsche’s supervisory board and that no changes were anticipated.

Porsche had already agreed to reduce its workforce by around 9,000 positions by 2035. The package includes 5,000 additional job reductions agreed in July, largely through natural attrition, early retirement and voluntary severance, following an earlier package of around 3,900 cuts and another 500 linked to subsidiary closures.

The restructuring comes as Porsche faces weaker sales in China, challenges with its electric vehicle strategy and pressure to reduce costs. The July agreement also included employment and site protections until 2035, alongside €2.1 billion in planned investment at its Zuffenhausen and Weissach sites.

Leiters’ latest communication therefore provides employees with clarity that the reported additional cuts are not part of Porsche’s current approved restructuring plan, even as the wider Volkswagen Group continues its cost-cutting efforts.
